data.name: Mythos: The Beginning - Director's Cut
data.detailed_description:
A terrifying horror RPG experience.

MYTHOS: THE BEGINNING is a survival horror role playing game based on the pulp-horror and monster movies of the 1930s. Set in London in 1934, Mythos tasks you with creating your own paranormal investigator from scratch and guiding them through a frightening exploration of the infamous Harborough Asylum. Three young university students have vanished while attempting to conduct a scientific survey of this dreaded place, and it's up to you to find them! Throughout the night you'll discover Harborough Asylum's reputation is more than an urban legend, and you'll have to fight for your life against otherworldly Lovecraftian foes.

Features:

  • Blends traditional survival horror gameplay with an old school tabletop-style RPG experience, complete with dialogue trees, non-combat skills and dice rolls.
  • Create your character from scratch. Choose their gender, background and profession, and then role play them. Will you be a square jawed investigator, or an intrepid journalist?
  • Pen and paper RPG inspired character advancement system. Levels are gone forever! Spend EXP directly to buy stats and skill increases.
  • Multiple ways to play the game! Don't want to fight the enemies? You don't have to! Gain EXP for correctly utilizing non-combat skills such as Persuade and Occult Lore.
  • A Terrifying Gothic Horror storyline that pays homage to the monster movie classics of the 1930s with meaningful choices and multiple endings to discover.

The Director's Cut edition also includes the following additional content:


  • Overhauled and rebalanced gameplay mechanics.
  • Tons of new skill checks and more ways to progress through the game.
  • New and rewritten dialogues.
  • New rooms containing new items and scares.
  • Edge of Madness expansion integrated into the base game.

reviews.review:
Developed by Dark Gaia Studios and published by KOMODO, Mythos: The Beginning - Director's Cut is an indie horror RPG that combines the eerie appeal of Lovecraftian fiction with the freedom of tabletop role-playing mechanics. Set in London in 1934, the game places players in the shoes of an investigator searching for three university students who vanished after venturing into the abandoned Harborough Asylum. The premise immediately establishes an atmosphere of uncertainty and dread, drawing inspiration from classic horror literature and early monster films while presenting a narrative-driven experience that favors exploration over spectacle.

One of the game's defining strengths is its emphasis on player agency. Character creation extends beyond cosmetic choices, allowing players to shape their investigator's background and abilities in ways that meaningfully affect progression. Instead of following a traditional leveling structure, experience is invested directly into attributes and skills, giving each playthrough a unique identity. Skills related to persuasion, research, and occult knowledge frequently unlock alternate dialogue options and solutions, making the player's choices feel consequential. This approach lends Mythos a tabletop sensibility that is uncommon among indie horror titles and encourages experimentation across multiple runs.

The setting of Harborough Asylum is easily the game's most memorable element. Every corridor and abandoned chamber contributes to a growing sense of unease, with environmental storytelling gradually revealing the institution's grim history. Tales of unethical experiments, unexplained deaths, and supernatural influences are woven into the narrative at a deliberate pace, allowing suspense to build naturally. Despite being built with RPG Maker, the game succeeds in creating an oppressive atmosphere through its writing, sound design, and carefully structured encounters. The asylum feels less like a backdrop and more like an active participant in the story, constantly reminding players that they are trespassing in a place better left forgotten.

Gameplay balances investigation, puzzle-solving, and occasional combat. Encounters with monsters and otherworldly threats are present, but they are rarely the central focus. In many cases, players can rely on dialogue skills or careful planning to avoid direct conflict altogether. This flexibility reinforces the game's role-playing foundation and prevents it from becoming a conventional action-horror experience. However, the slower pace may not appeal to everyone. Some segments involve backtracking, and a few puzzles can feel obscure by modern standards, requiring patience and close attention to environmental details.

The Director's Cut enhances the original release with additional content, revised mechanics, and improved balance. The inclusion of expanded story elements, extra locations, and the Edge of Madness content package makes this version feel more complete and polished. Dialogue revisions and new skill checks help strengthen player immersion, while the added content enriches both the world and its mysteries without overstaying its welcome. It is evident that Dark Gaia Studios revisited the project with a desire to refine their original vision rather than simply re-release it.

Visually, Mythos shows its age and the limitations of its development tools, but these shortcomings are mitigated by its strong artistic direction and commitment to atmosphere. Players expecting modern production values may find the presentation modest, yet those willing to embrace its retro aesthetic will discover a game with a distinct personality. The writing carries much of the experience, supported by a soundtrack that complements the unsettling tone and reinforces the feeling of isolation.

Mythos: The Beginning - Director's Cut is ultimately a niche title that knows exactly what audience it is targeting. It successfully blends survival horror, investigative storytelling, and role-playing mechanics into a cohesive package that rewards curiosity and thoughtful decision-making. While its pacing and dated presentation may limit its appeal to a broader audience, fans of Lovecraftian horror and classic RPG design will likely find its haunted halls and branching paths difficult to forget.

Rating: 6/10
